subject.title: Control UI settings pages need one unified design language

question: Should Control UI settings pages adopt the proposed flat section-and-row anatomy as the canonical standard, and which listed operational hubs may retain specialized layouts?
rationale: The design drift is source-backed, but selecting a mandatory visual anatomy, reconciling it with the documented glass system, and defining migration exceptions requires maintainer product and visual-design intent.

options.title: Approve staged standard
options.body: Adopt shared settings primitives and tokens, document narrow exceptions, and migrate related page families through several bounded pull requests.

options.title: Start with config surfaces
options.body: Standardize schema and quick-config pages first while leaving operational hubs on their current specialized layouts.

options.title: Retain principles only
options.body: Keep the existing broad design guidance and address inconsistencies opportunistically without enforcing one settings anatomy.

recommendation.title: Approve staged standard
recommendation.body: Adopt shared settings primitives and tokens, document narrow exceptions, and migrate related page families through several bounded pull requests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged design-system documentation and assignment to the earlier Control UI UX audit provide the strongest available ownership trail for this decision.
